sentences.text: A.Kamaraju vs State Of Ap on 6 August, 2019

Honourable Sri Justice D.V.S.S. Somayajulu
 Criminal Petition No.4625 of 2019
Order:

This criminal petition is filed under Sections 482 Cr.P.C., seeking to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.1135 of 2017 on the file of the Court of II Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Bhimavaram.

entities.text:
II Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Bhimavaram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The accused are charged of an offence under Sections 273 IPC Section 54 and 59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Section 7 of Cigarettes and Tobacco Act, 2003.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that as far as the offences under Section 273 IPC and Sections 54 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 are concerned, the same are quashed as they are covered by the decision of a learned single Judge of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, which was followed in other similar cases.

With regard to allegation under Section 7 of the COTPA Act, learned counsel submits that Section 7 deals with the sale of tobacco produces without a specified warning including a pictorial warning on the packing.
He points out that a reading of the charge sheet, the statements of the witnesses including LWs.3 and 4 does not disclose anything about the "lack" of such pictorial warning on the seized material.
Learned Public Prosecutor also does not really oppose the application.
This Court notices that a reading of the charge sheet does not disclose any offence under Section 7 of the COTPA Act is actually made out.
The charge sheet does not state anything about the lack of a pictorial warning on the material seized.
The witnesses who are examined also do not speak that the requisite pictorial warning is not there on the material.
In that view of the matter, this Court is of the opinion that no further useful purpose would be served by trying the accused under Section 7 of the COTPA Act.
The continuation of the prosecution would amount to an abuse of process of Court, hence, the same is quashed.
In the result, the criminal petition is allowed.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
__ D.V.S.S.SOMAYAJULU,J Date : 06.08.2019 KLP A.Kamaraju vs State Of Ap on 6 August, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133468253/
